A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network training experiments, Hessian and representation analyses, and numerical simulations of its toy models.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds optimizer experiments, synthetic regression experiments, and further analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix F extends the existing setup with the SignSGD update in Equation (23) and Adam-trained networks. This is a limited extension of training procedures; the centered networks, core architectures, losses, and original SGD models remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 primarily documents the existing parameterization.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds Gaussian single-index regression tasks with quadratic and scaled cubic targets, evaluated using MLPs. This extends coverage beyond the retained image-classification datasets and scalar toy simulations to nonlinear regression with multidimensional inputs.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated non-SGD optimizer comparators: SignSGD simulations in Figure 11 correspond to the original SGD toy-model experiments, while Adam CNN experiments in Figure 12 complement SGD experiments in Figure 10. This substantially broadens the optimizer comparison beyond v1.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce approximately 5% learning-rate warmup followed by cosine decay, including matched SGD and Adam CNN studies. Appendix G adds a synthetic-task protocol with width-consistency checks and phase portraits evaluated at 900 steps; Appendix O tests alternative learning-rate scaling rules. These are additional protocols, not established changes to the original runs.

E4.justification: New analyses test robustness to warmup and decay, compare alternative learning-rate exponents with the proposed scaling, and measure weight movement across layers, times, and three matrix norms. Appendix G also checks width consistency on synthetic tasks. These directly examine robustness and the interpretation of feature-learning strength.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-initialization error bars in Figure 2 and state that most MNIST-1M runs were repeated over three initialization seeds. v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure, significance test, or explicit increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 adds optimizer phase portraits, single-index results, alternative-scaling loss trajectories, and weight-movement results supporting gamma^(1/L) scaling after sufficient training. Figure 36(a) also adds an MNIST-1M MLP catapult example where v1 Figure 32(a) repeated a CIFAR-5M CNN example. The principal existing results and Table 1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix F derives SignSGD learning-rate exponents of gamma in the lazy regime and gamma^(1/L) in the ultra-rich regime, with matching upper and lower exponents. It argues that this removes SGD's finite triangle of optimizability and uses SignSGD to approximate Adam. This substantially extends the theoretical analysis; the original SGD derivations remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central SGD scaling laws, large-gamma performance claims, dynamical phenomena, and toy-model explanation. The appendix extensions do not materially redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F introduces an optimizer-dependent mechanism: rapid saddle escape is used to explain the absence of a finite optimizability triangle and silent alignment under SignSGD/Adam. It recommends Adam for ultra-rich investigations while explicitly leaving SignSGD catapult behavior unresolved. These are substantive new interpretations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies explicit muP/Depth-muP layer equations, global SGD learning-rate scaling, and Transformer attention-temperature scaling. Figure 6 newly specifies toy-model depth L=5, and the added experiments disclose schedules and synthetic-task configurations. Existing hardware, precision guidance, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Adam, SignSGD, and adaptive optimization at infinite width, and replaces the Tensor Programs VI citation with Yang and Littwin's adaptive-optimization work. The central positioning relative to lazy learning, feature learning, and online versus offline training remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose remains verbatim. Changes include new appendix subsections, localized explanatory additions and caption edits, updated cross-references, and affiliation, acknowledgment, and header edits. There is no extensive rewrite of the central narrative.

P2.justification: The appendices gain substantial visual material: optimizer and synthetic-task heatmaps, alternative-scaling trajectory comparisons, and weight-norm plots. A catapult panel is replaced, while retained figures are largely renumbered or repositioned. Figure 39 introduces a labeling inconsistency: its bottom-panel titles retain the alternative exponent although the caption identifies optimal scaling.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens understanding of the scaling laws' applicability through schedule controls, synthetic tasks, and paired optimizer analysis and experiments. Alternative-scaling and weight-movement checks also provide more direct support for the central explanation. The Adam interpretation remains heuristic, and some labels and the conclusion are inconsistently updated, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and explanatory scope.
